entity.name: Queen Victoria
entity.description: Grandmother of Europe who reigned for 63 years. Crowned at eighteen, Victoria married Prince Albert, had nine children who married into every royal house on the continent, and presided over an empire covering a quarter of the globe. After Albert's death she wore black for 40 years.

story.name: Queen Victoria
story.description: Born at Kensington Palace, crowned at eighteen, married her cousin Albert at the Chapel Royal, mourned him for decades at Osborne House, and died as Empress of India after 63 years on the throne.

moments.name: Victoria Is Born at Kensington Palace as Fifth in Line to the Throne
moments.subtitle: Within a year, two deaths will make the infant princess third in line
moments.description: On 24 May 1819 at 4:15 a.m., Princess Alexandrina Victoria was born at Kensington Palace in London, the only child of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, and Princess Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld. At birth she was fifth in line to the throne, behind four aging uncles. Her father died when she was eight months old, and her grandfather George III died a week later, pushing the infant to third in line. Raised in near-isolation under the strict "Kensington System" devised by her mother and the domineering comptroller John Conroy, Victoria shared a bedroom with her mother every night until she became queen at eighteen.

moments.name: Queen Victoria Marries Her Cousin Prince Albert at the Chapel Royal
moments.subtitle: The queen proposed to the prince, not the other way around
moments.description: On 10 February 1840, Queen Victoria married her maternal first cousin Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha at the Chapel Royal in St James's Palace, London. Because Victoria was the reigning monarch, she had to propose to Albert rather than wait for him to ask. The couple had nine children, who married into royal families across Europe, earning Victoria the nickname "grandmother of Europe." Albert became Victoria's closest political advisor and the driving force behind the Great Exhibition of 1851. When Albert died in 1861, Victoria wore black for the remaining 40 years of her life.
moments.address: Chapel Royal, St James's Palace, London

moments.name: Parliament Grants Victoria the Title Empress of India
moments.subtitle: Disraeli gifts a queen the subcontinent as a political masterstroke
moments.description: In 1876, the British Parliament passed the Royal Titles Act, granting Queen Victoria the additional title of Empress of India. The legislation was pushed through by Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli, who understood that Victoria craved the imperial title partly because her daughter had married the heir to the German Empire and would outrank her own mother. The title formalized British sovereignty over the Indian subcontinent, home to roughly 250 million subjects. Victoria never visited India, but the title became central to her identity. The proclamation ceremony took place on 1 January 1877 in Delhi, cementing the symbolic bond between the British Crown and its largest colonial possession.

moments.name: Victoria Celebrates Sixty Years on the Throne with a Diamond Jubilee
moments.subtitle: Troops from every corner of the empire parade through London
moments.description: On 22 June 1897, Queen Victoria celebrated her Diamond Jubilee, marking 60 years on the British throne — longer than any previous English or British monarch. The celebration was orchestrated as a festival of the British Empire: colonial premiers attended, and troops from every territory paraded through London. Victoria rode in an open carriage through six miles of streets lined by millions of spectators. Too frail to climb the steps of St Paul's Cathedral, the 78-year-old queen attended a short thanksgiving service held outside on the steps. The jubilee reinforced the monarchy's symbolic role at a time when real political power had shifted decisively to Parliament.

moments.name: Queen Victoria Dies at Osborne House After 63 Years on the Throne
moments.subtitle: The longest-reigning British monarch passes surrounded by children and grandchildren
moments.description: On 22 January 1901, Queen Victoria died at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight at the age of 81, ending a reign of 63 years and 216 days — the longest of any British monarch up to that time. Victoria had retreated to her beloved Osborne House, the Italianate palace she and Prince Albert had built together in the 1840s, and which she cherished as a private refuge from court life. Her death marked the end of the Victorian era, a period synonymous with industrial revolution, imperial expansion, and rigid social morality. She was succeeded by her 59-year-old son, who became Edward VII.
moments.address: Osborne House, East Cowes, Isle of Wight
